summary: Provision templated Oncall Runbook Confluence space + rotation-driven Slack channel orchestration
description:
Issue summary:
Request to create a reusable Confluence space template for team oncall runbooks and an automation that creates a temporary Slack channel + Jira incident project whenever a team rotation starts. The automation should provision channel permissions from the team's oncall groups, create a linked Confluence runbook page pre-populated from the template, and annotate the associated Jira project with the rotation metadata.

Impact:
- Reduces manual work when rotating oncall leads and ensures consistent runbook structure and permissions.
- Improve response time by ensuring channels and runbooks exist at rotation start.
- Potential security surface: automated channel creation requires granting a service account rights to create channels and invite groups.

Requirements / Acceptance criteria:
1) Confluence: a space template named "Oncall Runbook (templated)" with variables for Team, Rotation Start, Rotation End, Oncall Owner, PagerDuty schedule link, escalation paths, runbook sections (triage, mitigation, rollback, postmortem notes). Template must include a macro to display linked Jira INC- issues.
2) Slack: automation that creates channels with naming convention #oncall-<team>-<YYYYMMDD>-<rotation-id> and sets channel topic to include rotation owner and Confluence runbook link. Channels should be auto-archived after the rotation end + 30 days.
3) Permissions: channel membership should be inherited from existing SSO groups: team-<team>-oncall and team-<team>-eng. The provisioning flow must require an approver from Security or Platform for teams classified as "restricted".
4) Jira: create a light-weight Jira project/issue template for incident coordination that is automatically created and linked to the channel and runbook when requested.
5) Auditability: every automated action must produce an audit log entry (Confluence page created, Slack channel created, Jira project/issue created) with the service-account identity and rotation metadata.
6) Rollback & safety: provisioning should support dry-run mode and a manual approval step for first 5 team rollouts; provide a revoke action that removes channel invites and unlinks the runbook but preserves artifacts for postmortem.

Requested by: Platform Engineering on behalf of multiple pods.

Notes on scope and constraints:
- Prefer implementing automation via existing internal provisioning API (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/tree/main/provisioning) rather than new bots, reusing service-account and scoped OAuth tokens.
- Security requires a short (30d) token rotation window for the service account used; consult IAM for least-privilege role.
- Confluence template must be created in the "Platform Runbooks" parent space and use page properties for automated indexing.

Suggested rollout plan:
- Phase 1: Build template and a manual provisioning playbook that SRE/Platform can run to create the first 3 team runbook spaces and channels (dry-run mode available).
- Phase 2: Implement automation with approval gating for restricted teams. Document RBAC and IAM required.
- Phase 3: Gradual enablement for all teams; add metrics (time-to-provision, number of created channels, manual approvals) to Console.
